study.name: RELIEF
study.label: RELIEF Study
study.description: A Phase 2 Single-Arm, Multicenter, Exploratory Safety and Efficacy Study of IF001 to Remove Long-Term Immunosuppression from Prior Living Donor Kidney Transplant Recipients. This is a multicenter, open-label, single-arm proof-of-concept study to demonstrate the safety and efficacy of IF001 in adult participants 3 to 62 months following transplantation of a kidney from a living donor. The study will enroll 15 participants, with no more than 6 who are HLA-matched, to meet a target of 12 participants with complete follow-up. Study participants will receive chemotherapy and radiation therapy prior to IF001 cell therapy, then GVHD prophylaxis with high-dose, post-IF001 infusion cyclophosphamide, prednisone, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate mofetil. Study participation will last approximately 27 months from Screening through Follow-up.

population.description: Adult participants aged 18 to 50 years who have received a kidney transplant from a partially or fully HLA-matched living donor 3 to 62 months prior to signing informed consent. Participants must be matched with the kidney donor for at least 4 alleles of HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-C, and HLA-DRB1 genes and at least one matched allele of the HLA-DRB-1 gene. Participants must have stable renal allograft function ≥ 45 mL/min/1.73 m2 prior to screening. The living donor must be 18 to 50 years of age, willing to undergo mobilization and apheresis, and meet all eligibility criteria for stem cell donation.

studyVersion.description: This is a Phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm proof-of-concept study evaluating IF001, a cell therapy product containing CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells and αβ TCR cells, in adult kidney transplant recipients 3 to 62 months post-transplantation. The study aims to demonstrate safety and efficacy of IF001 in removing long-term immunosuppression while preventing graft loss and rejection. Participants receive conditioning therapy followed by IF001 infusion from their original living kidney donor, with follow-up through Month 15 for primary analysis and extended evaluation through Month 24. The study will enroll 15 participants across multiple US centers, with no more than 6 fully HLA-matched participants, targeting 12 participants with complete follow-up.

indication.name: End-stage kidney failure requiring kidney transplantation
indication.description: Kidney transplantation is the preferred mode of renal replacement therapy for patients with end-stage kidney failure because it provides better quality of life compared with dialysis and prolongs patient survival. Despite advances in immunosuppressive medications that have reduced acute rejection risk and extended patient and allograft survival, chronic immunosuppression imposes tremendous burden on patients requiring life-long daily medication adherence, significant adverse effects, and high costs. Adverse events related to chronic immunosuppressive therapy include progression of cardiovascular disease, increased susceptibility to infection, metabolic abnormalities, neurologic disorders, and greater risk of malignancy. Late acute cellular rejection and chronic antibody-mediated rejection remain problematic, with nearly one third of kidney allografts lost within 10 years. Contemporary management includes high-dose immunosuppressive drugs at transplant followed by life-long daily maintenance treatment, which may result in substantial side effects including nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, and metabolic derangements while often not completely controlling immune system damage to the kidney.

studyArm.name: Single Treatment Arm
studyArm.label: IF001 Treatment Arm
studyArm.description: This is a single-arm study where all participants receive the same treatment regimen. Participants are adult recipients of kidney transplants from living donors who received their transplant 3 to 62 months prior to enrollment. All participants undergo reduced intensity conditioning consisting of Thymoglobulin, fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, and total body irradiation, followed by IF001 infusion on Day 1. Post-infusion treatment includes cyclophosphamide for GVHD prophylaxis, tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, prednisone, and filgrastim. The study enrolls 15 participants total, with no more than 6 who are fully HLA-matched, targeting 12 participants with complete follow-up. Participants are followed for 15 months for the primary study period with extended evaluation through Month 24.

studyEpoch.name: Screening
studyEpoch.description: Screening evaluations performed from Day −90 to Day −10. Includes inclusion/exclusion criteria verification, demographics, medical history, physical exam, electrocardiogram, pulmonary function tests, height, vital signs including weight, safety panel, urine protein/creatinine ratio, pregnancy test for women of childbearing potential, vaccine antibody titers, baseline reference chimerism, HLA typing, DSA, infectious disease screening, and immunosuppression with MMF and tacrolimus. Participants who signed informed consent but failed screening will have completed CRFs for screening period, demographics, screen failure details, eligibility criteria, and any SAE data collected.
studyEpoch.label: Screening Period

studyEpoch.name: Conditioning
studyEpoch.description: Conditioning period from Day −9 through Day −1. Includes vital signs, safety panel, urine protein/creatinine ratio, pregnancy test, vaccine antibody titers, immunosuppression with MMF and tacrolimus, PRO assessments, thymoglobulin (ATG) on Days −9 through −7, fludarabine on Days −6 through −2, cyclophosphamide 14.5 mg/kg on Days −6 and −5, and total body irradiation on Day −1. Before conditioning can begin, adequate reference donor and participant chimerism samples must be available, participant must have negative local DSA result, and IF001 must have been received at clinical site.
studyEpoch.label: Conditioning Period

studyEpoch.name: Treatment
studyEpoch.description: Treatment period from Days 1 through 6. Includes daily safety panel until ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days, urine protein/creatinine ratio on Day 1, pregnancy test on Day 1, bacterial/fungal prophylaxis daily until ANC >500 cells/µL, viral prophylaxis daily, IF001 infusion on Day 1, cyclophosphamide 50 mg/kg and Mesna 10 mg/kg IBW on Days 4 and 5, filgrastim administration starting Day 6 until ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days, immunosuppression with MMF and tacrolimus starting Day 6, and prednisone starting Day 6.
studyEpoch.label: Treatment Period

studyEpoch.name: Initial Follow-up
studyEpoch.description: Initial follow-up period from Days 7 through 14. Continues daily safety panel until ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days, bacterial/fungal prophylaxis until ANC >500 cells/µL, viral prophylaxis daily, filgrastim administration until ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days, immunosuppression with MMF and tacrolimus, prednisone, BKV and CMV monitoring on Day 8, local tacrolimus level starting Day 9 daily until ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days, and dialysis as needed.
studyEpoch.label: Initial Follow-up

studyEpoch.name: Follow-Up Period
studyEpoch.description: Follow-up period from Day 15 through Month 24. Includes physical exam at Months 9, 12, and 15, bacterial/fungal prophylaxis until ANC >500 cells/µL, viral prophylaxis until Day 183 (recommended until Month 12), pneumocystis prophylaxis starting Day 22 or after ANC >500 cells/µL, vital signs including weight, safety panel, urine protein/creatinine ratio, CD4 count at Day 183 and Month 9, immunoglobulins at Day 183 and Month 9, local blood typing at Month 12, DSA at multiple timepoints, HAMA sample at Day 57, immunosuppression as needed, local tacrolimus level as needed, filgrastim as needed, and BKV and CMV monitoring.
studyEpoch.label: Follow-Up Period

studyEpoch.name: Extended Evaluation
studyEpoch.description: Extended evaluation period after Month 15 until Month 24. Participants will complete visits at Months 18 and 24 for extended follow-up analysis of Months >15 through 24. The Extended Analysis Set (EAS) consists of all participants who have at least one visit between Month >15 and Month 24. Extended evaluation endpoints include incidence of composite endpoint of BPAR, graft loss or death, incidence of graft loss, death, lost to follow-up, acute rejection, treated BPAR by Banff 2022 criteria, de novo DSA, donor chimerism correlation to being off IS, and incidence and grade of acute and chronic GVHD.
studyEpoch.label: Extended Evaluation

studyElement.name: Inspection of Records
studyElement.label: Record Inspection
studyElement.description: The sponsor will be allowed to conduct site visits to the investigation facilities for the purpose of monitoring any aspect of the study. The investigator agrees to allow the monitor to inspect the investigational product storage area and accountability records, participant charts, study source documents, and other records relative to study conduct.

studyElement.name: Site Monitoring
studyElement.label: Site Monitoring
studyElement.description: Before the study starts, at a site initiation visit or at an investigator's meeting, a sponsor representative and/or designee will review the protocol and CRFs with the investigators and their staff. During the study, the sponsor will ensure compliance with the protocol and Good Clinical Practice (GCP) as well as the quality and integrity of the data at each site. The Clinical Research Associate (CRA) will visit the site to check the completeness of participant records, the accuracy of entries on the CRFs, the adherence to the protocol, and to GCP, the progress of enrollment, and to ensure that investigational product is being stored, administered, and accounted for according to specifications.

studyElement.name: Study Completion and Site Closure
studyElement.label: Site Closure
studyElement.description: Upon completion of the study, the monitor will conduct activities including return of all study data to the sponsor, data queries, accountability and reconciliation of investigational product, review of study records for completeness, and reconciliation of Investigator Site File and Trial Master File.

studyElement.name: Access to Information for Audits and Inspections
studyElement.label: Audit Access
studyElement.description: Authorized representatives of the sponsor, a regulatory authority, or an IRB may visit the site to perform audits or inspections, including source data verification. The purpose is to systematically and independently examine all study-related activities and documents to determine whether these activities were conducted, and data were recorded, analyzed, and accurately reported according to the protocol, GCP, and any applicable regulatory requirements.

studyElement.name: Retention of Records
studyElement.label: Record Retention
studyElement.description: The Principal Investigator must maintain all documentation relating to the study for a period of 2 years after the last marketing application approval, or if not approved, 2 years following the discontinuance of the test article for investigation. If it becomes necessary for the sponsor or a regulatory authority to review any documentation relating to the study, the investigator must permit access to such records.

studyElement.name: Publication and Data Sharing Policy
studyElement.label: Publication Policy
studyElement.description: No data collected as part of the study will be utilized in any written work, including publications, without the written consent of the sponsor. The sponsor will post key design elements of this protocol in a publicly accessible database such as clinicaltrials.gov. Upon study completion and finalization of the study report, the results of the trial will be either submitted for publication and/or posted in a publicly accessible database of clinical trial results.

studyDesignPopulation.name: Kidney Transplant Recipients for Tolerance Induction
studyDesignPopulation.description: The study population consists of kidney transplant recipients who will receive IF001, an investigational cell therapy product containing defined doses of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells and αβ TCR cells for induction of transplantation tolerance. Recipients must have received a kidney transplant from the same donor who will provide the stem cells. The study will enroll 15 participants empirically determined to provide adequate safety, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy data while exposing as few participants as possible to study procedures. Participants will undergo a reduced intensity conditioning regimen including Thymoglobulin, fludarabine, cyclophosphamide, and total body irradiation, followed by IF001 infusion and post-infusion cyclophosphamide for GVHD prophylaxis. The population includes both HLA-matched and partially HLA-matched donor-recipient pairs, with different TBI doses based on matching status (200 cGy for HLA-matched, 400 cGy for partially HLA-matched). All participants must provide informed consent and meet specific inclusion and exclusion criteria. The study aims to achieve transplantation tolerance allowing withdrawal of immunosuppressive therapy while maintaining graft function.

activity.name: Physical Examination
activity.label: Physical Examination
activity.description: Physical examinations will include Karnofsky performance status, general appearance, head/eyes/ears/nose/throat, lungs, cardiac, abdominal, skin, extremities, lymph nodes, and a neurologic examination. In addition to the protocol-specified times, physical assessments can be made at the investigator's discretion to evaluate symptoms or AEs.

activity.name: Vital Signs Including Height and Weight
activity.label: Vital Signs Assessment
activity.description: Vital sign assessments include blood pressure and pulse rate performed by the same study site staff member using the same validated device. Blood pressure and pulse rate will be assessed in the same arm each time after the participant has rested in the sitting position for at least 5 minutes. Systolic and diastolic blood pressure will be measured using an automated validated device with an appropriately sized cuff. The sitting measurements will be repeated at 1- to 2-minute intervals for a total of 3 measurements. Participants should be weighed without shoes or coat using the same scale. Height will be measured only at the first screening visit.

activity.name: Electrocardiogram
activity.label: 12-lead ECG
activity.description: A 12-lead electrocardiogram will be conducted at screening for all participants.

activity.name: Pulmonary Function Tests
activity.label: Pulmonary Function Tests
activity.description: Pulmonary function tests including FEV1 and FVC will be conducted at screening for all participants.

activity.name: Laboratory Assessments
activity.label: Laboratory Assessments
activity.description: Local and central laboratories will be used for analysis of specimens collected as described in the schedules of assessments. Clinical laboratory tests can also be performed as medically indicated. Clinical laboratory assessments include complete blood count with white blood cell differential, comprehensive metabolic panel, infectious disease screening, pregnancy testing, viral load monitoring, vaccine antibody titers, urinalysis, HLA typing, donor-specific antibody testing, ABO blood typing and Rh factor, donor whole blood and blood T cell chimerism, tacrolimus trough levels, HAMA sample, and immunoglobulins.

activity.name: BKV and CMV Monitoring
activity.label: Viral Load Monitoring
activity.description: BKV and CMV infection monitoring is by local measurement of quantitative viral load by a PCR-based method. BK virus and CMV monitoring are performed more frequently than scheduled visits: Weekly through Day 183 (Month 6), every 2 weeks thereafter through Month 12, and every 3 months through Month 15.

activity.name: GVHD Assessment
activity.label: GVHD Assessment
activity.description: Beginning at Day 22 through Day 92, only acute GVHD assessments will be performed. At Day 92 and Day 120, both acute and chronic GVHD assessments will be performed. Beyond Day 120, chronic GVHD assessments will be performed routinely, but acute GVHD also can be assessed as clinically warranted. If acute or chronic GVHD is suspected or detected at any time between visits, appropriate GVHD assessment must be performed at an unscheduled visit. Sites should supplement with weekly telephone contact through Day 183. Grading of GVHD should follow the criteria provided in appendices for acute GVHD and chronic GVHD.

activity.name: Renal Allograft Biopsy
activity.label: Kidney Biopsy
activity.description: Kidney allograft protocol biopsies are to be performed and analyzed centrally at Day 160 and at Month 15. Site-specific protocol/surveillance biopsies without suspicion of acute rejection are prohibited. Biopsies will be read by the local pathologist according to the updated Banff 2022 criteria and the results recorded on the relevant CRF. The local results will be used for the management of acute rejection. Central pathology diagnosis will be used for analysis of efficacy endpoints.

activity.name: Patient-Reported Outcome Measures
activity.label: PRO Assessments
activity.description: The impact of IF001 on the participants' quality of life will be assessed by the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) and the End-Stage Renal Disease Symptom Checklist (ESRD-SCL). The questionnaires should be completed by participants at the clinic before seeing the study physician. Participants should be given sufficient instruction, space, time, and privacy to complete the questionnaire. Study staff should check the questionnaire responses for completeness. Before the clinical examination, completed questionnaires will be reviewed by the investigator for responses that might indicate possible AEs or SAEs.

activity.name: Bacterial/Fungal Prophylaxis
activity.label: Antimicrobial Prophylaxis
activity.description: Bacterial and fungal prophylaxis must be provided at least from Day 1 until the ANC >500 cells/µL.

activity.name: Viral Prophylaxis
activity.label: Viral Prophylaxis
activity.description: Herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus prophylaxis must be provided from Day 1 until Day 183 and is recommended until Month 12. For participants who are IgG (+) for CMV and participants who are IgG (−) for CMV but who received a kidney from a donor who is IgG (+), it is recommended that CMV prophylaxis be provided from Day 1 until Day 92.

activity.name: Pneumocystis Prophylaxis
activity.label: PCP Prophylaxis
activity.description: Pneumocystis prophylaxis (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia/pneumocystis carinii pneumonia) must be provided starting on Day 22 or after the ANC is >500 cells/µL, whichever occurs later.

activity.name: IF001 Infusion
activity.label: IF001 Infusion
activity.description: IF001 infusion is administered on Day 1 of the treatment phase.

activity.name: Cyclophosphamide Administration
activity.label: Post-infusion Cyclophosphamide
activity.description: Cyclophosphamide 50 mg/kg and Mesna 10 mg/kg IBW administered on Days 4 and 5. Mesna 10 mg/kg IBW to be given 30 minutes before and 3, 6, and 8 hours before the Day 4 and Day 5 cyclophosphamide doses.

activity.name: Filgrastim Administration
activity.label: G-CSF Administration
activity.description: Filgrastim (G-CSF) or a biosimilar given intravenously or subcutaneously 5 µg/kg/day (rounded to nearest vial size) should be administered starting on Day 6 until the ANC is >1000 cells/µL for 3 days. Additional G-CSF may be administered as warranted. Pegfilgrastim (Neulasta) and GM-CSF are not permitted.

activity.name: Immunosuppression Administration
activity.label: Immunosuppressive Therapy
activity.description: Tacrolimus should be started on Day 6 (at least 24 hours after the completion of post-transplantation cyclophosphamide). The MMF dose will start on Day 6 and may be discontinued after the last dose on Day 36. MMF dosing may continue if active GVHD is present. Prednisone is administered starting Day 6.

activity.name: Tacrolimus Level Monitoring
activity.label: Tacrolimus Level Assessment
activity.description: The recipient should withhold the morning tacrolimus dose until after the blood draw to obtain a trough level. Beginning on Day 9, levels should be assessed daily until the ANC is >1000 cells/µL for 3 days. Thereafter tacrolimus levels should be assessed 3 days after any dose adjustment.

activity.name: Thymoglobulin Administration
activity.label: ATG Administration

scheduleTimeline.name: Screening and Conditioning
scheduleTimeline.description: Screening phase occurs from Day -90 through -10, followed by conditioning from Day -9 through Day -1. Screening includes inclusion/exclusion criteria verification, demographics, medical history, physical exam, electrocardiogram, pulmonary function tests, height, vitals, safety panel, urine protein/creatinine ratio, pregnancy test for WOCBP, vaccine antibody titers, baseline reference chimerism, HLA typing, DSA, infectious disease screening, and immunosuppression management. Conditioning includes thymoglobulin (ATG) on Days -9, -8, -7, fludarabine on Days -6 through -2, cyclophosphamide 14.5 mg/kg on Days -6 and -5, and total body irradiation on Day -1. Last dose of pre-transplantation mycophenolate mofetil is Day -10 and last dose of pre-transplantation tacrolimus is Day -4.
scheduleTimeline.label: Screening and Conditioning Phase

scheduleTimeline.name: Treatment and Initial Follow-Up
scheduleTimeline.description: Treatment phase spans Days 1 through 6, followed by initial follow-up Days 7 through 14. Day 1 includes IF001 infusion, safety panel, urine protein/creatinine ratio, pregnancy test for WOCBP, and initiation of bacterial/fungal and viral prophylaxis. Post-transplantation cyclophosphamide 50 mg/kg with Mesna 10 mg/kg IBW administered on Days 4 and 5. Filgrastim administration begins Day 6 and continues daily until ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days. Immunosuppression with MMF and tacrolimus starts Day 6, along with prednisone. Daily safety panels continue until ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days. BKV and CMV monitoring begins Day 8. Local tacrolimus levels monitored daily starting Day 9 until ANC >1000 cells/µL for 3 days.
scheduleTimeline.label: Treatment and Initial Follow-Up

scheduleTimeline.name: Follow-Up Period
scheduleTimeline.description: Extended follow-up from Day 15 through Month 24 with specific visit windows. Key visits include D15, D22, D29, D36, D43, D50, D57, D92, D120, D160, D183, Month 9, Month 12, Month 15, early termination, Month 18, and Month 24. Assessments include physical exams at Month 12 and 15, vital signs and safety panels at all visits, urine protein/creatinine ratio at specified intervals, CD4 count and immunoglobulins at Day 183 and Month 12, DSA monitoring starting Day 160, GVHD assessments from Day 22 onwards, kidney allograft biopsies at Day 160 and Month 15, donor chimerism monitoring, and PRO assessments at Month 12 and 15. Prophylaxis continues with bacterial/fungal until ANC >500 cells/µL, viral prophylaxis until Day 183, and pneumocystis prophylaxis starting Day 22. Immunosuppression weaning may begin as early as Day 183 if criteria are met.
scheduleTimeline.label: Follow-Up Period

studyIntervention.label: IF001 Cell Therapy
studyIntervention.description: IF001 is an investigational cell therapy product containing defined doses of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells and αβ TCR cells for induction of transplantation tolerance in recipients of kidney transplants from the same donor. The cryopreserved product contains a minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient IBW (no maximum) and a target of 10 million αβ TCR cells per kg of recipient IBW (range 8-12 million per kg). IF001 is administered intravenously through a large bore central venous catheter on Day 1. The product is derived from mobilized peripheral blood cells collected by apheresis from the intended kidney donor and is manufactured, cryopreserved, and stored prior to shipping to the study center for thawing and infusion.

studyIntervention.label: Reduced Intensity Conditioning
studyIntervention.description: Participants receive a reduced intensity conditioning regimen starting 9 days prior to IF001 infusion consisting of: Thymoglobulin on Days -9 (0.5 mg/kg IV over 6 hours), -8 (2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours), and -7 (2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours); Fludarabine on Days -6, -5, -4, -3 and -2 (30 mg/m2 IV daily, dose adjusted for kidney function); Cyclophosphamide on Day -6 and Day -5 (14.5 mg/kg IV daily, total dose 29 mg/kg); and a single fraction of total body irradiation on Day -1 (200 cGy for HLA-matched cohort and 400 cGy for partially HLA-matched cohort).

studyIntervention.label: Post-infusion Cyclophosphamide
studyIntervention.description: Cyclophosphamide (50 mg/kg IV daily) is administered on Day 4 and Day 5 for GVHD prophylaxis following IF001 infusion. Mesna (sodium 2-mercaptoethane sulfonate) is administered with cyclophosphamide to minimize potential toxicity. Cyclophosphamide and Mesna are dosed based on ideal body weight, unless actual body weight is less than ideal body weight. Participants must be given Mesna 10 mg/kg IBW 30 minutes before and 3, 6, and 8 hours before the Day 4 and Day 5 cyclophosphamide doses.

studyIntervention.label: Immunosuppressive Therapy
studyIntervention.description: Tacrolimus IV or oral is started on Day 6 and administered to a target level of 8 to 12 ng/mL. MMF is dosed at 15 mg/kg of actual body weight orally 3 times daily up to 1 g TID and discontinued after Day 36. Prednisone 10 mg orally daily is initiated on Day 6 with the last dose on Day 36. Participant immunosuppression may be tapered as early as Day 183 if criteria are met including T cell chimerism >50%, no active GVHD, no evidence of de novo DSA, and absence of biopsy-proven acute rejection. Tacrolimus is reduced by ≥50% by Month 9 and discontinued at Month 12.

studyIntervention.label: Infection Prophylaxis
studyIntervention.description: Bacterial prophylaxis is provided from Day 1 until absolute neutrophil count is >500 cells/µL (example: moxifloxacin 400 mg per day). Fungal prophylaxis with mold coverage is provided from Day 1 until ANC >500 cells/µL (example: posaconazole 300 mg daily). Herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus prophylaxis is provided from Day 1 until Day 183 (example: valacyclovir 500 mg twice daily). CMV prophylaxis is recommended from Day 1 until Day 92 for at-risk participants (example: letermovir 480 mg once daily). Pneumocystis prophylaxis starts on Day 22 or after ANC >500 cells/µL (example: trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 single strength tablet daily).

studyIntervention.label: Filgrastim Support
studyIntervention.description: Filgrastim (G-CSF) or a biosimilar is given IV or subcutaneously starting on Day 6 for IF001 recipients at 5 µg/kg/day of actual body weight (rounded to nearest vial size) until the absolute neutrophil count is >1000 cells/µl for 3 days. Additional G-CSF may be administered as warranted. Pegfilgrastim (Neulasta) and granulocyte-macrophage-CSF are not permitted.

administration.label: IF001 Infusion
administration.description: On Day 1, IF001 will be administered intravenously through a large bore central venous catheter. A dialysis-specific catheter/shunt should NOT be used for IF001 administration. The recipient should be carefully monitored during and after infusion to detect any changes indicative of hypersensitivity and infusion-related reactions. The infusion will be performed at the recipient's bedside. Premedication with corticosteroids (100 mg hydrocortisone), diphenhydramine, and acetaminophen should be performed as prophylaxis against adverse infusion-related side effects per institutional guidelines. The thawing procedure, infusion volume, date, and start and stop time will be documented.

administration.label: DMSO Reaction Management
administration.description: Cryopreserved products, including IF001, contain dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO). When the product is thawed and infused, DMSO may cause nausea and/or headache. If reported by the recipient, reduce the rate of infusion and administer ondansetron and/or diphenhydramine (if indicated). Wait 10-15 minutes before thawing and infusing subsequent bags of donor cells. If a moderate to severe reaction occurs, immediately contact the Medical Monitor.

administration.label: Tacrolimus Administration
administration.description: Tacrolimus IV or oral (oral immediate-release administration preferred) should be started on Day 6 (at least 24 hours after the completion of post-transplantation cyclophosphamide) and administered as per institutional standards to a target level of 8 to 12 ng/mL. The recommended IV starting dose is 0.03 mg/kg/day either as a continuous infusion or divided into 12-hour IV bolus dosing based on ABW. Oral equivalent dosing is acceptable at a suggested starting dose of 0.05 to 0.1 mg/kg/dose orally twice daily. If a participant converts from IV to oral once therapeutic levels are achieved, a suggested IV to oral conversion of 1:3 can be used or per institutional standards.

administration.label: MMF Administration
administration.description: The MMF dose will be 15 mg/kg of ABW orally 3 times daily (TID) up to 1 g TID (or IV equivalent) or an equimolar dose of MPS. The MMF dose will be discontinued after the last dose on Day 36 or may continue if active GVHD is present. Equimolar doses of enteric-coated MPS (Myfortic® or equivalent) may be substituted for MMF. When switching from MMF immediate-release to MPS delayed-release tablets, the equimolar doses of free mycophenolic acid content are: 250 mg MMF = 180 mg MPS; 500 mg MMF = 360 mg MPS.

administration.label: Prednisone Administration
administration.description: Prednisone 10 mg orally daily will be initiated on Day 6 with the last dose on Day 36, unless the participant was on chronic oral steroids prior to enrollment. If a participant was taking daily corticosteroids for >90 days prior to study enrollment, weaning of corticosteroids to prevent adrenal insufficiency is allowed per institutional standard or clinical judgement, provided that corticosteroids are withdrawn prior to Month 9. An example weaning schedule is provided starting with prednisone 5mg daily on Days 36 to 57, then gradually reducing to 0.5mg every other day from Days 241 to Month 9, then discontinue.

administration.label: Pneumocystis Prophylaxis
administration.description: Pneumocystis prophylaxis (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia/pneumocystis carinii pneumonia) must be provided starting on Day 22 or after the ANC is >500 cells/µL, whichever occurs later. If the CD4 count at the Day 183 visit is >200 cells/µL, the pneumocystis prophylaxis may be discontinued. If the CD4 count is ≤ 200 cells/µL, the agent should be continued until the CD4 count check at Month 12, after which investigator judgement can determine whether to continue or discontinue prophylaxis. Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 single strength tablet daily is the preferred example, with atovaquone 1500 mg once daily or dapsone 100 mg once daily as alternatives.

substance.label: IF001
substance.description: IF001 is a cryopreserved allogeneic somatic cell therapy product derived from donor mobilized peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The cellular product contains defined doses of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells and alpha/beta positive T-cell receptor (αβ TCR) cells for induction of transplantation tolerance in recipients of kidney transplants from the same donor. The product contains a minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient ideal body weight (no maximum) and a target of 10 million αβ TCR cells per kg of recipient ideal body weight (range 8-12 million per kg). IF001 is administered as a one-time intravenous infusion through a large bore central venous catheter, given 3 to 62 months after living donor kidney transplant.

substance.label: Thymoglobulin
substance.description: Thymoglobulin (anti-thymocyte globulin) is administered as part of the conditioning regimen on Days -9, -8, and -7. The dosing is 0.5 mg/kg intravenously over 6 hours on Day -9, followed by 2 mg/kg intravenously over 4 hours on Days -8 and -7. Preparations of anti-thymocyte globulin other than Thymoglobulin are excluded from the protocol.

substance.label: Fludarabine
substance.description: Fludarabine is administered as part of the conditioning regimen on Days -6, -5, -4, -3, and -2 at a dose of 30 mg/m2 intravenously daily. The dose is adjusted for kidney function as part of the reduced intensity conditioning regimen.

substance.label: Cyclophosphamide
substance.description: Cyclophosphamide is administered at two different doses during the protocol. During conditioning, it is given at 14.5 mg/kg intravenously daily on Days -6 and -5. Post-transplantation, it is administered at 50 mg/kg intravenously daily on Days 4 and 5. Mesna 10 mg/kg ideal body weight is given 30 minutes before and 3, 6, and 8 hours after the Day 4 and Day 5 cyclophosphamide doses.

substance.label: Tacrolimus
substance.description: Tacrolimus is started on Day 6 (at least 24 hours after completion of post-transplantation cyclophosphamide) and administered per institutional standards to target a level of 8 to 12 ng/mL. The last dose of pre-transplantation tacrolimus is given on Day -4. If tacrolimus is not tolerated, cyclosporine may be substituted. Tacrolimus levels are assessed daily until the absolute neutrophil count is >1000 cells/µL, then 3 days after any dose adjustment.

substance.label: Mycophenolate mofetil
substance.description: Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) is administered at 15 mg/kg of actual body weight orally 3 times daily up to 1 g three times daily (or intravenous equivalent) or an equimolar dose of mycophenolic acid sodium. The last dose of pre-transplantation MMF is on Day -10. Post-transplantation MMF starts on Day 6 and is discontinued after the last dose on Day 36, or may continue if active graft-versus-host disease is present.

substance.label: Prednisone
substance.description: Prednisone 10 mg orally daily is initiated on Day 6 with the last dose on Day 36 as part of the graft-versus-host disease prophylaxis regimen.

substance.label: Filgrastim
substance.description: Filgrastim (granulocyte colony-stimulating factor) or a biosimilar is given intravenously or subcutaneously starting on Day 6 at 5 µg/kg/day of actual body weight (rounded to nearest vial size) until the absolute neutrophil count is >1000 cells/µL for 3 days. Additional G-CSF may be administered as warranted. Pegfilgrastim (Neulasta) and granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor are not permitted.

substance.label: Mesna
substance.description: Mesna is administered at 10 mg/kg ideal body weight to be given 30 minutes before and 3, 6, and 8 hours after the Day 4 and Day 5 cyclophosphamide doses as a protective agent.

substance.label: Cyclosporine
substance.description: Cyclosporine may be substituted for tacrolimus if tacrolimus is not tolerated. It is administered intravenously or orally starting on Day 6 per institutional standards to maintain a level of 200 to 400 ng/mL (high-pressure liquid chromatography method) or 250 to 500 ng/mL (immunoassay method). Recommended starting doses range from 3 to 6 mg/kg/day intravenous bolus dosing every 12 hours or 6 mg/kg/day orally divided twice daily.

substance.label: Sirolimus
substance.description: Sirolimus with a target concentration of 10 ng/ml may be substituted for participants intolerant of or experiencing unacceptable toxicity from calcineurin inhibitors.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Graft-versus-Host Disease
BiomedicalConcept.description: GVHD is considered an adverse event of special interest. Beginning at Day 22 through Day 92, only acute GVHD assessments will be performed. At Day 92 and Day 120, both acute and chronic GVHD assessments will be performed. Beyond Day 120, chronic GVHD assessments will be performed routinely, but acute GVHD also can be assessed as clinically warranted. Grading of GVHD should follow the criteria provided in Appendix 2 for acute GVHD (Harris 2016) and Appendix 3 for chronic GVHD (Jagasia 2015). All Grade ≥2 acute GVHD or moderate to severe chronic GVHD must be reported within 24 hours of site awareness.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Biopsy-Proven Acute Rejection
BiomedicalConcept.description: A BPAR is defined as a biopsy result with either T cell-mediated rejection of Banff Grade ≥1A OR acute/active antibody-mediated rejection (local pathology reading according to the Banff 2022 criteria). Renal biopsies will be performed for all cases of suspected acute rejection and at specified protocol visits. Suspicion of acute rejection is deferred to the clinical investigator and local practices. An example would be: an acute and persistent increase in serum creatinine by ≥20% and/or new onset or worsening proteinuria, with other potential causes ruled out.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Renal Function
BiomedicalConcept.description: Renal function by estimated eGFR using the CKD-EPI 2021 formula will be derived from local laboratory creatinine values. This will also be the primary method of assessment of renal function with respect to other renal endpoints. The 2021 CKD-EPI Creatinine formula is: 142 × (Scr/A)B × 0.9938age × (1.012 if female), where A and B values differ by gender and serum creatinine levels.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Graft Loss
BiomedicalConcept.description: The allograft will be presumed to be lost on the day the participant starts dialysis and is subsequently unable to be removed from dialysis for 56 consecutive days or if the participant is retransplanted. If the participant undergoes allograft nephrectomy prior to starting permanent dialysis, then the day of nephrectomy is the day of graft loss. Graft loss is considered an SAE and should be reported as described in Section 7.4.2.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Donor Chimerism
BiomedicalConcept.description: Whole blood and T cell chimerism require a whole blood sample. The proportion of donor chimerism as defined as ≥50% T-cell chimerism will be calculated with 95% CI (exact binomial) for the FAS. The proportion of participants who were successfully able to wean off IS without BPAR or graft loss at Month 15 among those with donor chimerism will be calculated with 95% CI (exact binomial).

BiomedicalConcept.label: Donor-Specific Antibodies
BiomedicalConcept.description: DSA specimens should be drawn and tested locally at the time of any suspected rejection. Specimens for DSA should also be drawn and tested locally at Month 12 post-IF001 infusion and whenever a blood transfusion is given. The incidence of DSA will be analyzed in the same manner as BPAR. The incidence of de novo DSA is evaluated at Day 183, Month 12, and Month 15.

BiomedicalConcept.label: BK Virus Infection
BiomedicalConcept.description: BKV infection monitoring is by local measurement of quantitative viral load by a PCR-based method. BK virus monitoring is performed more frequently than scheduled visits: Weekly through Day 183 (Month 6), every 2 weeks thereafter through Month 12, and every 3 months through Month 15. The incidence of BK viremia, viruria, infection, and nephropathy is evaluated at Day 183, Month 12, and Month 15.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Cytomegalovirus Infection
BiomedicalConcept.description: CMV infection monitoring is by local measurement of quantitative viral load by a PCR-based method. CMV monitoring is performed more frequently than scheduled visits: Weekly through Day 183 (Month 6), every 2 weeks thereafter through Month 12, and every 3 months through Month 15. For participants who are IgG (+) for CMV and participants who are IgG (−) for CMV but who received a kidney from a donor who is IgG (+), it is recommended that CMV prophylaxis be provided from Day 1 until Day 92.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Off Immunosuppression
BiomedicalConcept.description: A participant will be considered free from IS if they are not currently taking any IS agents and have not taken IS since withdrawal. An exception will be brief use of systemic corticosteroids for no more than 8 weeks (total duration) if administered for an indication other than rejection prophylaxis or treatment (such as newly developed or recurrent autoimmune diseases, asthma, hypersensitivity reactions). After complete weaning of immunosuppression additional serum creatinine should be performed locally weekly for 4 weeks.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Adverse Events
BiomedicalConcept.description: An AE is any untoward medical occurrence (ie, any unfavorable and unintended sign [including abnormal laboratory findings], symptom, or disease) in a participant or clinical investigation participant after providing written informed consent for participation in the study. Severity will be assessed per the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) v 6.0 Grade 1 through Grade 5. The investigator must assess the relationship of each AE/SAE with the use of the investigational product IF001.

BiomedicalConcept.label: Serious Adverse Events
BiomedicalConcept.description: An SAE is defined as any AE which meets any one of the following criteria: Is fatal, life-threatening, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, constitutes a congenital anomaly/birth defect, requires inpatient hospitalization or prolongation of existing hospitalization (with specific exceptions), or is medically significant. All malignant neoplasms will be assessed as serious under 'medically significant' if other seriousness criteria are not met. Every SAE must be reported to the sponsor or designee within 24 hours of learning of its occurrence.

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Normal Biopsy
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Category 1 of Banff 2022 criteria representing normal biopsy or nonspecific changes. Requires exclusion of any diagnosis from the Banff Diagnostic Categories 2-4, 6.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: CATEGORY 1: Normal Biopsy Or Nonspecific Changes

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Active AMR
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Active antibody-mediated rejection requiring all 3 criteria: active lesions of AMR (microvascular inflammation, intimal/transmural arteritis, or acute thrombotic microangiopathy), evidence of complement activation or microvascular inflammation, and circulating donor-specific antibodies to HLA or other antigens.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Active AMR; All 3 criteria must be met for diagnosis

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Chronic Active AMR
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Chronic active antibody-mediated rejection requiring all 3 criteria: chronic lesions of AMR including transplant glomerulopathy or severe peritubular capillary basement membrane multilayering, identical to criterion 2 for active AMR, and identical to criterion 3 for active AMR including strong recommendation for DSA testing.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Chronic active AMR; all 3 criteria must be met for diagnosis

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Chronic AMR
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Chronic antibody-mediated rejection requiring all 3 criteria: cg > 0 and/or severe ptcml, absence of criterion 2 as defined for active and chronic active AMR, and prior documented diagnosis of active or chronic active ABMR and/or documented prior or current evidence of DSA.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Chronic AMR; all 3 criteria must be met for diagnosis

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: C4d Staining Without Rejection
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: C4d staining without evidence of rejection requiring all 4 features: linear C4d staining in peritubular capillaries, criterion 1 for active or chronic active AMR not met, negative biopsy-based transcript diagnostics for AMR/MVI, and no acute or chronic active TCMR or borderline changes.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: C4d staining without evidence of rejection; all 4 features must be met for diagnosis

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: MVI DSA-negative C4d-negative
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Microvascular inflammation/injury that is DSA-negative and C4d-negative requiring all 3 criteria: at least moderate microvascular inflammation, no linear C4d staining in peritubular capillaries, and no serologic evidence of circulating donor-specific antibodies.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Microvascular inflammation/injury (MVI), DSA-negative and C4d-negative; all 3 criteria must be met for diagnosis

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Probable AMR
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Probable antibody-mediated rejection requiring all 4 criteria: identical to criterion 1 for active AMR, criterion 1 for chronic active and chronic AMR not met, absence of criterion 2 defined for active and chronic active AMR, and identical to criterion 3 for active AMR but C4d must be negative.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Probable AMR; all 4 criteria must be met for diagnosis

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: C4d Staining with ATI
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: C4d staining with acute tubular injury requiring all 3 criteria: acute tubular injury is present, linear C4d staining in peritubular capillaries, and criterion 1 for active or chronic active AMR not met.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: C4d staining with acute tubular injury (ATI); all 3 criteria must be met for diagnosis

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Borderline TCMR
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Category 3 representing suspicious (borderline) for acute T-cell mediated rejection with foci of Banff Lesion Score t>0 AND Banff Lesions Score i=1 OR Foci of Banff Lesion Score t1 AND Banff Lesion Score i ≥ 2.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: CATEGORY 3: Suspicious (Borderline) For Acute TCMR

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Acute TCMR IA
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Acute T-cell mediated rejection grade IA with Banff Lesion Score i ≥ 2 AND Banff Lesion Score t2.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Acute TCMR IA Banff Lesion Score i ≥ 2 AND Banff Lesion Score t2

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Acute TCMR IB
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Acute T-cell mediated rejection grade IB with Banff Lesion Score i ≥ 2 AND Banff Lesion Score t3.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Acute TCMR IB Banff Lesion Score i ≥ 2 AND Banff Lesion Score t3

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Acute TCMR IIA
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Acute T-cell mediated rejection grade IIA with Banff Lesion Score v1 regardless of Banff Lesion Scores i or t.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Acute TCMR IIA Banff Lesion Score v1 regardless of Banff Lesion Scores i or t

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Acute TCMR IIB
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Acute T-cell mediated rejection grade IIB with Banff Lesion Score v2 regardless of Banff Lesion Scores i or t.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Acute TCMR IIB Banff Lesion Score v2 regardless of Banff Lesion Scores i or t

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Acute TCMR III
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Acute T-cell mediated rejection grade III with Banff Lesion Score v3 regardless of Banff Lesion Scores i or t.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Acute TCMR III Banff Lesion Score v3 regardless of Banff Lesion Scores i or t

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Chronic Active TCMR IA
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Chronic Active T-cell mediated rejection Grade IA with Banff Lesion Score ti ≥ 2 AND Banff Lesion Score i-IFTA ≥ 2, other known causes of i-IFTA ruled out AND Banff Lesion Score t2.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Chronic Active TCMR Grade IA Banff Lesion Score ti ≥ 2 AND Banff Lesion Score i-IFTA ≥ 2, other known causes of i-IFTA (eg, pyelonephritis, BK-virus nephritis etc.) ruled out AND Banff Lesion Score t2

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Chronic Active TCMR IB
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Chronic Active T-cell mediated rejection Grade IB with Banff Lesion Score ti ≥ 2 AND Banff Lesion Score i-IFTA ≥ 2, other known causes of i-IFTA ruled out AND Banff Lesion Score t3.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Chronic Active TCMR Grade IB Banff Lesion Score ti ≥ 2 AND Banff Lesion Score i-IFTA ≥ 2, other known causes of i-IFTA ruled out AND Banff Lesion Score t3

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Chronic Active TCMR II
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Chronic Active T-cell mediated rejection Grade II characterized by arterial intimal fibrosis with mononuclear cell inflammation in fibrosis and formation of neointima.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Chronic Active TCMR Grade II Arterial intimal fibrosis with mononuclear cell inflammation in fibrosis and formation of neointima

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: IFTA Grade I
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy Grade I (Mild) with Banff Lesion Score ci1 OR Banff Lesion Score ct1.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Grade I (Mild) Banff Lesion Score ci1 OR Banff Lesion Score ct1

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: IFTA Grade II
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy Grade II (Moderate) with Banff Lesion Score ci2 OR Banff Lesion Score ct2.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Grade II (Moderate) Banff Lesion Score ci2 OR Banff Lesion Score ct2

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: IFTA Grade III
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy Grade III (Severe) with Banff Lesion Score ci3 OR Banff Lesion Score ct3.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: Grade III (Severe) Banff Lesion Score ci3 OR Banff Lesion Score ct3

BiomedicalConceptCategory.label: Other Changes
BiomedicalConceptCategory.description: Category 6 representing other changes not considered to be caused by acute or chronic rejection including Polyomavirus Nephropathy, Posttransplant Lymphoproliferative Disorder, Calcineurin Inhibitor Toxicity, Acute Tubular Injury, Recurrent Disease, De Novo Glomerulopathy, Pyelonephritis, and Drug-Induced Interstitial Nephritis.
BiomedicalConceptCategory.text: CATEGORY 6: Other Changes Not Considered To Be Caused By Acute Or Chronic Rejection

Procedure.name: Physical Examination
Procedure.label: Physical Examination
Procedure.description: Physical examinations will include Karnofsky performance status, general appearance, head/eyes/ears/nose/throat, lungs, cardiac, abdominal, skin, extremities, lymph nodes, and a neurologic examination. In addition to the protocol-specified times, physical assessments can be made at the investigator's discretion to evaluate symptoms or AEs.

Procedure.name: Vital Signs Including Height and Weight
Procedure.label: Vital Signs Assessment
Procedure.description: Vital sign assessments (blood pressure and pulse rate) should be performed by the same study site staff member using the same validated device. Blood pressure and pulse rate will be assessed in the same arm each time after the participant has rested in the sitting position for at least 5 minutes. Systolic and diastolic blood pressure will be measured using an automated validated device with an appropriately sized cuff. The sitting measurements will be repeated at 1- to 2-minute intervals for a total of 3 measurements. Participants should be weighed without shoes or coat using the same scale. Height (without shoes) will be measured only at the first screening visit.

Procedure.name: Electrocardiogram
Procedure.label: 12-lead ECG
Procedure.description: A 12-lead electrocardiogram will be conducted at screening for all participants.

Procedure.name: Pulmonary Function Tests
Procedure.label: Pulmonary Function Tests
Procedure.description: Pulmonary function tests including FEV1 and FVC will be conducted at screening for all participants.

Procedure.name: Revaccination
Procedure.label: Revaccination Schedule
Procedure.description: The recommendations for vaccination after allogeneic HCT are based on the guidelines of the Infectious Disease Society of America and are summarized in Appendix 1.

Procedure.name: Laboratory Assessments
Procedure.label: Laboratory Assessments
Procedure.description: Local and central laboratories will be used for analysis of specimens collected as described in the schedules of assessments. Clinical laboratory tests can also be performed as medically indicated. BKV and CMV infection monitoring is by local measurement of quantitative viral load by a PCR-based method. BK virus and CMV monitoring are performed more frequently than scheduled visits: Weekly through Day 183, every 2 weeks thereafter through Month 12, and every 3 months through Month 15. All laboratory test results considered clinically significant by the investigator will be followed to a satisfactory resolution.

Procedure.name: Renal Function Assessment
Procedure.label: Renal Function Assessment
Procedure.description: Renal function by estimated eGFR using the CKD-EPI 2021 formula will be derived from local laboratory creatinine values. This will also be the primary method of assessment of renal function with respect to other renal endpoints.

Procedure.name: Graft-versus-Host-Disease Assessment
Procedure.label: GVHD Assessment
Procedure.description: Beginning at Day 22 through Day 92, only acute GVHD assessments will be performed. At Day 92 and Day 120, both acute and chronic GVHD assessments will be performed. Beyond Day 120, chronic GVHD assessments will be performed routinely, but acute GVHD also can be assessed as clinically warranted. If acute or chronic GVHD is suspected or detected at any time between visits, appropriate GVHD assessment must be performed at an unscheduled visit. Sites should supplement with weekly telephone contact through Day 183. Grading of GVHD should follow the criteria provided in Appendix 2 for acute GVHD and Appendix 3 for chronic GVHD.

Procedure.name: Renal Allograft Biopsy
Procedure.label: Kidney Biopsy
Procedure.description: Kidney allograft protocol biopsies are to be performed and analyzed centrally at Day 160 and at Month 15. Site-specific protocol/surveillance biopsies without suspicion of acute rejection are prohibited. Biopsies will be read by the local pathologist according to the updated Banff 2022 criteria and the results recorded on the relevant CRF. The local results will be used for the management of acute rejection. Central pathology diagnosis will be used for analysis of efficacy endpoints. Renal biopsies will be performed for all cases of suspected acute rejection and at specified protocol visits.

Procedure.name: Patient-Reported Outcome Measures
Procedure.label: PRO Assessments
Procedure.description: The impact of IF001 on the participants' quality of life will be assessed by the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36) and the End-Stage Renal Disease Symptom Checklist (ESRD-SCL). The questionnaires should be completed by participants at the clinic before seeing the study physician. Participants should be given sufficient instruction, space, time, and privacy to complete the questionnaire. Study staff should check the questionnaire responses for completeness and encourage the participant to provide any missing responses. The responses from the paper questionnaire will be entered into the CRF by study staff.

Procedure.name: Obtaining Informed Consent
Procedure.label: Informed Consent
Procedure.description: Signed informed consent will be obtained from the participant before any study procedures are undertaken. Details regarding the informed consent process and documentation are provided in Section 13.2.

Procedure.name: Medical History
Procedure.label: Medical History
Procedure.description: Medical history findings (ie, previous diagnoses, diseases, or surgeries) not pertaining to the study indication, started before signing the informed consent and during the screening phase, and considered relevant for the participant's study eligibility will be collected and captured in the CRF.

analysisPopulation.label: Full Analysis Set
analysisPopulation.description: The FAS consists of all participants who initiate the conditioning regimen. This set will include follow-up until Month 15. The FAS will be used as the efficacy analysis set to evaluate both primary and secondary efficacy endpoints of participants. The FAS will be used for all participant safety analyses, unless otherwise specified.

analysisPopulation.label: Per Protocol Analysis Set
analysisPopulation.description: The PPAS consists of all participants in the FAS who complete the IF001 infusion, comply with treatment and follow-up as described in the protocol, and either meet an endpoint or complete the 15-month treatment period with no major protocol deviations. All efficacy and safety endpoints will also be performed using the PPAS.

analysisPopulation.label: Extended Analysis Set
analysisPopulation.description: The EAS consists of all participants who have at least one visit between Month >15 and Month 24. The EAS will be used for secondary extended follow-up analyses. The EAS will be summarized for Month >15 to Month 24.

Organization.name: ImmunoFree, Inc.
Organization.label: Sponsor
Organization.description: ImmunoFree, Inc. is the sponsor company for this Phase 2 clinical trial studying IF001, an investigational cryopreserved allogeneic somatic cell therapy derived from donor mobilized peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The company is conducting a single-arm, multicenter study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of IF001 for removing long-term immunosuppression from prior living donor kidney transplant recipients.

Organization.name: Emmes
Organization.label: Data Management CRO
Organization.description: Emmes is contracted by the sponsor to manage the Advantage eClinical data system being used for this study. The Principal Investigator and at least 2 staff from each site must complete training requirements and obtain access to this electronic data capture system managed by Emmes. Forms not entered into Advantage eClinical within specified time will be considered delinquent, and missing forms will continue to be requested until entered into the master database at Emmes or until an exception is granted by Emmes staff.

Organization.name: National Marrow Donor Program
Organization.label: Donor Management Organization
Organization.description: The National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP) has been contracted by the sponsor to manage the donation process and donor follow-up. Donors will undergo stem cell mobilization, stem cell collection, and follow-up according to NMDP standard procedures. The NMDP criteria for stem cell transplantation must be met for all donors participating in this study.

Organization.name: Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research
Organization.label: CIBMTR Registry
Organization.description: The Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) is a registry organization where centers participating in this study must register pre- and post-HCT outcomes. Registration is done using procedures and forms of the Stem Cell Transplant Outcomes Database. Federal legislation requires submission of these forms for all United States allotransplant recipients. The CIBMTR forms will be submitted directly to the CIBMTR through routine CIBMTR mechanisms.

studyRole.name: Principal Investigator
studyRole.label: Principal Investigator
studyRole.description: The Principal Investigator must maintain all documentation relating to the study for a period of 2 years after the last marketing application approval, or if not approved, 2 years following the discontinuance of the test article for investigation. The Principal Investigator and at least 2 staff from each site will need to complete training requirements and obtain access to the electronic data capture system. The investigator must maintain source documents for each participant in the study and keep all original informed consent documents signed by the participant.

studyRole.name: Clinical Research Associate
studyRole.label: Clinical Research Associate
studyRole.description: The Clinical Research Associate (CRA) will visit the site to check the completeness of participant records, the accuracy of entries on the CRFs, the adherence to the protocol, and to GCP, the progress of enrollment, and to ensure that investigational product is being stored, administered, and accounted for according to specifications. The CRA must have access to all relevant source documents to confirm their consistency with the CRF entries. The monitor will be available between visits if the investigator(s) or other staff need information or advice.

studyRole.name: Medical Monitor
studyRole.label: Medical Monitor
studyRole.description: At the investigator's discretion and following discussion with the Medical Monitor, an extension of screening may be granted under extenuating circumstances such as a death in the family or serious illness.

studyRole.name: Emmes Staff
studyRole.label: Emmes Staff
studyRole.description: The data system being used for this study is Advantage eClinical® managed by Emmes, contracted by the sponsor. A missing form will continue to be requested either until the form is entered into Advantage eClinical and integrated into the master database at Emmes, or until an exception is granted by Emmes staff and entered into the Missing Form Exception File.

studyRole.name: Sponsor Representative
studyRole.label: Sponsor Representative
studyRole.description: Before the study starts, at a site initiation visit or at an investigator's meeting, a sponsor representative and/or designee will review the protocol and CRFs with the investigators and their staff. The sponsor will be allowed to conduct site visits to the investigation facilities for the purpose of monitoring any aspect of the study.

studySite.label: Multiple US Centers
studySite.description: This is a multicenter study conducted at multiple centers in the United States. The study will enroll 15 participants across these centers, with no more than 6 who are HLA-matched, to meet a target of 12 participants with complete follow-up. Each study center must meet clinical site criteria for stem cell transplantation, and all participants must meet the clinical site criteria for stem cell transplantation. The sponsor has contracted with the National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP) to manage the donation process and donor follow-up at participating sites.
studySite.name: Multiple centers in the United States

GeographicScope.name: United States
GeographicScope.description: The study will be conducted at multiple centers in the United States. This is a multicenter, open-label, single-arm proof-of-concept study to demonstrate the safety and efficacy of IF001 in adult participants 3 to 62 months following transplantation of a kidney from a living donor.

narrativeContent.name: Data System
narrativeContent.description: The data system being used for this study is Advantage eClinical® managed by Emmes, contracted by the sponsor. The Principal Investigator and at least 2 staff from each site will need to complete training requirements and obtain access to this electronic data capture system.

narrativeContent.name: Case Report Forms
narrativeContent.description: Criteria for timeliness of submission for all study forms are detailed in the eCRF Completion Guide and Advantage eClinical User's Guide. Forms that are not entered into Advantage eClinical within the specified time will be considered delinquent.

narrativeContent.name: Criteria for Forms Submission
narrativeContent.description: A missing form will continue to be requested either until the form is entered into Advantage eClinical and integrated into the master database at Emmes, or until an exception is granted by Emmes staff and entered into the Missing Form Exception File, as detailed in the Advantage eClinical User's Guide.

narrativeContent.name: Reporting Participant Deaths
narrativeContent.description: Participant death information must be entered into Advantage eClinical within 24 business hours of knowledge of the participant's death. If the cause of death is unknown at that time, it does not need to be recorded at that time. However, once the cause of death is determined, the Death Form must be updated in Advantage eClinical.

narrativeContent.name: CIBMTR Data Reporting
narrativeContent.description: Centers participating in this study must register pre- and post-HCT outcomes to the CIBMTR. Registration is done using procedures and forms of the Stem Cell Transplant Outcomes Database. Federal legislation requires submission of these forms for all United States allotransplant recipients. The CIBMTR forms will be submitted directly to the CIBMTR through routine CIBMTR mechanisms.

narrativeContent.name: Primary Objectives
narrativeContent.description: Safety: Determine the safety and tolerability of IF001 in previously transplanted recipients of a kidney from a living donor. Efficacy: Evaluate the efficacy of IF001 in preventing graft loss and BPAR following removal of pharmacologic IS.

narrativeContent.name: Secondary Objectives
narrativeContent.description: Safety objectives include characterizing the incidence and grade of acute GVHD by Day 120, severity of chronic GVHD by one-year post-IF001 infusion, incidence of BK viremia, viruria, infection, and nephropathy by 15 months post-IF001 infusion, and various other safety parameters. Efficacy objectives include evaluating changes in renal function from Day −9 to Month 15, time to composite events, donor chimerism correlation, and outcomes in participants with transient chimerism.

narrativeContent.name: Data Quality Assurance
narrativeContent.description: Sponsor staff and/or its designee review the data entered in the CRFs by investigational site staff for completeness and accuracy and instruct the site personnel to make any required corrections or additions. Concomitant medications will be coded using the World Health Organization Drug Reference List with Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification system. Concomitant procedures, non-drug therapies, and AEs will be coded using MedDRA terminology.

narrativeContent.name: Protocol Adherence
narrativeContent.description: This protocol defines the study objectives, study procedures, and data to be collected on study participants. Investigators must apply due diligence to avoid protocol deviations; all significant deviations will be recorded and reported in the clinical study report. Any protocol deviation for safety reasons must be considered a protocol amendment and requires sponsor approval.

narrativeContent.name: Protocol Amendments
narrativeContent.description: Any change or addition to the protocol can only be made in a written protocol amendment that must be approved by the sponsor and the IRB prior to implementation. Only amendments intended to eliminate an apparent immediate hazard to participants can be implemented immediately, provided health authorities are subsequently notified and the reviewing IRB is notified.

narrativeContent.name: Ethics
narrativeContent.description: This clinical study was designed and will be implemented and reported in accordance with ethical principles that have their origin in the Declaration of Helsinki, International Conference on Harmonization GCP, and all applicable regulatory requirements.

narrativeContent.name: Institutional Review Board
narrativeContent.description: Before the study starts, the investigator and institution must obtain IRB approval for the protocol, ICF, recruitment materials and procedures, and any other written information provided to potential participants. Written IRB approval must be submitted to the sponsor prior to enrolling a participant into the study. The Principal Investigator must sign the Investigator's Agreement and inform the IRB of any protocol amendments.

narrativeContent.name: Informed Consent
narrativeContent.description: The Principal Investigator will ensure that the patient is given full and adequate oral and written information about the nature, purpose, and possible risks and benefits of the study. Women of childbearing potential should be informed about unknown risks to the fetus and must adhere to contraception requirements. The participant's signed and dated informed consent must be obtained before conducting any study procedures. Donor informed consent will be obtained by the NMDP.

narrativeContent.name: Participant and Data Confidentiality
narrativeContent.description: After the ICF has been signed, each participant will be assigned a unique identifier. To ensure confidentiality of records and personal data of participants, any participant records or datasets transferred to the sponsor will only include the identifier. The participant must be informed that personal study-related data will be used by the sponsor in accordance with local data protection law and that medical records may be examined by research quality assurance auditors, IRB members, and regulatory inspectors.

narrativeContent.name: Inspection of Records
narrativeContent.description: The sponsor will be allowed to conduct site visits to the investigation facilities for the purpose of monitoring any aspect of the study. The investigator agrees to allow the monitor to inspect the investigational product storage area and accountability records, participant charts, study source documents, and other records relative to study conduct.

narrativeContent.name: Site Monitoring
narrativeContent.description: Before the study starts, a sponsor representative will review the protocol and CRFs with investigators and staff. During the study, the sponsor will ensure compliance with the protocol and GCP as well as data quality and integrity at each site. The Clinical Research Associate will visit sites to check completeness of participant records, accuracy of CRF entries, adherence to protocol and GCP, enrollment progress, and proper investigational product handling.

narrativeContent.name: Study Completion and Site Closure
narrativeContent.description: Upon completion of the study, the monitor will conduct activities including return of all study data to the sponsor, data queries, accountability and reconciliation of investigational product, review of study records for completeness, and reconciliation of Investigator Site File and Trial Master File.

narrativeContent.name: Access to Information for Audits and Inspections
narrativeContent.description: Authorized representatives of the sponsor, a regulatory authority, or an IRB may visit the site to perform audits or inspections, including source data verification. The purpose is to systematically and independently examine all study-related activities and documents to determine whether these activities were conducted and data were recorded, analyzed, and accurately reported according to the protocol, GCP, and applicable regulatory requirements.

narrativeContent.name: Retention of Records
narrativeContent.description: The Principal Investigator must maintain all documentation relating to the study for a period of 2 years after the last marketing application approval, or if not approved, 2 years following the discontinuance of the test article for investigation. If it becomes necessary for the sponsor or a regulatory authority to review any documentation relating to the study, the investigator must permit access to such records.

narrativeContent.name: Publication and Data Sharing Policy
narrativeContent.description: No data collected as part of the study will be utilized in any written work, including publications, without the written consent of the sponsor. The sponsor will post key design elements of this protocol in a publicly accessible database such as clinicaltrials.gov. Upon study completion and finalization of the study report, the results of the trial will be either submitted for publication and/or posted in a publicly accessible database of clinical trial results.

statisticalAnalysis.name: Primary and Secondary Statistical Analysis
statisticalAnalysis.label: Statistical Analysis Plan
statisticalAnalysis.description: Statistical methods were not taken into consideration in determining the sample size. The primary efficacy endpoint will be summarized using a point estimate along with its 95% confidence interval (CI) (exact binomial). Participants who are not free from IS at Month 15 or having BPAR, or graft loss, or death will be considered non-responders. The key secondary efficacy variable is the change in renal function (eGFR by CKD-EPI 2021), from baseline (Day −9, prior to the first dose of transplantation conditioning) to Month 15. Because this is a proof-of-concept study, no hypothesis tests will be conducted on the key secondary efficacy endpoint. Categorical endpoints will be summarized using counts and proportions. Endpoints with continuous variables will be summarized descriptively (non-missing values, means, standard deviations, medians, 25% and 75% quartiles, minimums, and maximums).
statisticalAnalysis.primaryModel: Descriptive statistics with 95% confidence intervals (exact binomial)

assumptions.source: Assuming a 20% dropout rate, it is anticipated that 15 participants will be enrolled, with no more than 6 who are fully HLA-matched, to meet the target of 12 participants with complete follow-up

concomitantMedications.name: Concomitant Medications
concomitantMedications.label: Study Concomitant Medications
concomitantMedications.description: All medications, procedures, and significant non-drug therapies administered after the participant has signed the study informed consent form will be recorded on the relevant case report form. The investigator should instruct the participant to notify the study site about any new medications, including non-prescription supplements, taken after study enrollment. Concomitant medications entered into the database will be coded using the World Health Organization Drug Reference List, which employs the Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical classification system.

permitted.name: Bacterial Prophylaxis
permitted.description: Bacterial prophylaxis must be provided at least from Day 1 until the absolute neutrophil count (ANC) is >500 cells/µL. Specific antibacterials may be given according to center practice. An example is moxifloxacin 400 mg per day.

permitted.name: Fungal Prophylaxis
permitted.description: Fungal prophylaxis must be provided from Day 1 until the ANC is >500 cells/µL. Specific antifungals may be given according to center practice and investigator judgement but must include coverage of molds such as Aspergillus. An example is posaconazole 300 mg daily.

permitted.name: Viral Prophylaxis
permitted.description: Herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus prophylaxis must be provided from Day 1 until Day 183 and is recommended until Month 12. Specific antivirals may be given according to center practice and investigator judgement. An example is valacyclovir 500 mg twice a day. For participants who are immunoglobulin G (IgG) (+) for CMV and participants who are IgG (−) for CMV but who received a kidney from a donor who is IgG (+), it is recommended that CMV prophylaxis be provided from Day 1 until Day 92. An example is letermovir 480 mg once daily.
permitted.condition: From Day 1 until Day 183 (recommended until Month 12)

permitted.name: Pneumocystis Prophylaxis
permitted.description: Pneumocystis prophylaxis (Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia/pneumocystis carinii pneumonia) must be provided starting on Day 22 or after the ANC is >500 cells/µL, whichever occurs later. If the CD4 count at the Day 183 visit is >200 cells/µL, the pneumocystis prophylaxis may be discontinued. If the CD4 count is ≤ 200 cells/µL, the agent should be continued until the CD4 count check at Month 12. Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 single strength tablet daily is the preferred example, with atovaquone 1500 mg once daily or dapsone 100 mg once daily as alternatives.
permitted.condition: Starting Day 22 or after ANC >500 cells/µL, whichever occurs later

permitted.name: Premedication for IF001 Infusion
permitted.description: Premedication with corticosteroids (100 mg hydrocortisone), diphenhydramine, and acetaminophen should be performed as prophylaxis against adverse infusion-related side effects per institutional guidelines.

permitted.name: Infusion Reaction Management
permitted.description: If nausea and/or headache are reported by the recipient due to DMSO, reduce the rate of infusion and administer ondansetron and/or diphenhydramine (if indicated). Wait 10-15 minutes before thawing and infusing subsequent bags of donor cells.
permitted.condition: During IF001 infusion if reactions occur

permitted.name: Brief Systemic Corticosteroids
permitted.description: Brief use of systemic corticosteroids for no more than 8 weeks (total duration) if administered for an indication other than rejection prophylaxis or treatment (such as newly developed or recurrent autoimmune diseases, asthma, hypersensitivity reactions).
permitted.condition: For indications other than rejection prophylaxis or treatment, maximum 8 weeks total duration

prohibited.name: Non-Thymoglobulin ATG Preparations
prohibited.description: Preparations of anti-thymocyte globulin (ATG) other than Thymoglobulin are excluded from the conditioning regimen and are not permitted during the study.

prohibited.name: Pegfilgrastim (Neulasta)
prohibited.description: Pegfilgrastim (Neulasta®) is not permitted during the study. Filgrastim (G-CSF) or a biosimilar should be used instead for granulocyte colony-stimulating factor support.

prohibited.name: Granulocyte-macrophage-CSF
prohibited.description: Granulocyte-macrophage-CSF is not permitted during the study. Filgrastim (G-CSF) or a biosimilar should be used instead for granulocyte colony-stimulating factor support.

dataMonitoringCommittee.name: Data Safety Monitoring Board
dataMonitoringCommittee.label: DSMB
dataMonitoringCommittee.description: An independent DSMB will be instituted at study initiation and will advise the sponsor and investigators on matters relating to the safety and conduct of the study. The DSMB will be governed by a charter that will include meeting frequency, stopping rules, and event triggers necessitating an unscheduled review. The DSMB will oversee the safety and risk/benefit of the study and follow stopping rules as defined in the DSMB Charter. Further enrollment into the study will be temporarily halted by the sponsor for a full DSMB safety assessment if specific safety thresholds are met, including severe acute GVHD, BPAR, infusion reactions, neutropenia, organ toxicity, or any death or graft loss. The DSMB will critically assess the background and clinical course of events leading to the temporary halt of the study as soon as possible.
dataMonitoringCommittee.mandate: Advise the sponsor and investigators on matters relating to the safety and conduct of the study
