cellTherapyManufacturing.name: IF001 Cell Therapy Manufacturing
cellTherapyManufacturing.label: IF001 Manufacturing Process
cellTherapyManufacturing.description: IF001 is an investigational cell therapy product containing defined doses of CD34+ hematopoietic stem cells and alpha/beta positive T-cell receptor (αβ TCR) cells for induction of transplantation tolerance in recipients of kidney transplants from the same donor. The cryopreserved product contains a minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient IBW (no maximum) and a target of 10 million αβ TCR cells per kg of recipient IBW (range 8-12 million per kg). Freshly harvested donor stem cells are immediately transported to the manufacturing center where the IF001 product is manufactured, cryopreserved, and stored prior to shipping to the study center for thawing and infusion into the participant. The IF001 product must pass applicable release criteria and is shipped frozen to the treating center prior to Day −9.
cellTherapyManufacturing.collectionProcedure: granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) mobilization and apheresis
cellTherapyManufacturing.collectionTiming: The same living kidney donor will undergo G-CSF mobilization and apheresis to generate the IF001 product
cellTherapyManufacturing.minimumStemCellYield: minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient IBW
cellTherapyManufacturing.manufacturingNotes: Donors will undergo stem cell mobilization, stem cell collection, and follow-up according to NMDP standard procedures. The sponsor has contracted with the National Marrow Donor Program (NMDP) to manage the donation process and donor follow-up.

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Thymoglobulin
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: Anti-thymocyte globulin conditioning
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: Thymoglobulin (anti-thymocyte globulin) administered as part of the reduced intensity conditioning regimen. Given on Days -9 (0.5 mg/kg intravenously over 6 hours), -8 (2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours), and -7 (2 mg/kg IV over 4 hours). Preparations of anti-thymocyte globulin other than Thymoglobulin are excluded from the protocol.

agents.name: Thymoglobulin
agents.dose: 0.5 mg/kg on Day -9, 2 mg/kg on Days -8 and -7

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Fludarabine
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: Fludarabine conditioning therapy
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: Fludarabine administered on Days -6, -5, -4, -3 and -2 at 30 mg/m2 IV daily, with dose adjusted for kidney function. Dosed on body surface area based upon recipient's actual body weight if <125% of IBW. For participants >125% of IBW, dosed on adjusted IBW. For participants with estimated or measured creatinine clearance <70 mL/min/1.73 m2, prior brain radiation, or prior intrathecal chemotherapy, the dose should be reduced by 20%.

agents.name: Fludarabine
agents.dose: 30 mg/m2 IV daily (dose adjusted for kidney function)

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Pre-transplantation Cyclophosphamide
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: Pre-transplant cyclophosphamide
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: Cyclophosphamide administered on Day -6 and Day -5 at 14.5 mg/kg IV daily as part of the conditioning regimen. Pre-transplantation cyclophosphamide administered as a 1- to 2-hour infusion with total dose received 29 mg/kg over the two days.

lymphodepletingChemotherapy.name: Total Body Irradiation
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.label: Single fraction TBI
lymphodepletingChemotherapy.description: A single fraction of total body irradiation (TBI) treatment administered on Day -1. Dose is 200 cGy for the HLA-matched cohort and 400 cGy for the partially HLA-matched cohort. The TBI dose selection is based on the trial of DeZern et al. where the first 7 patients received 200 cGy TBI with 3 graft failures and 2 deaths, leading to dose increase to 400 cGy for subsequent patients.

immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.name: Acute GVHD Monitoring
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.label: Acute GVHD Assessment
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.description: Monitoring for acute graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) with characterization of incidence and grade by Day 120 post-IF001 infusion. All Grade >2 acute GVHD will be reported within 24 hours of site awareness as an adverse event of special interest (AESI). Evaluation includes assessment at Day 183, Month 12, and Month 15 for incidence and grade of acute GVHD.
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.notes: Grade >2 acute GVHD reported as AESI within 24 hours

immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.name: Chronic GVHD Monitoring
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.label: Chronic GVHD Assessment
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.description: Monitoring for chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) with characterization of incidence and severity by one-year post-IF001 infusion. Any chronic GVHD will be reported within 24 hours of site awareness as an adverse event of special interest (AESI). Evaluation includes assessment at Day 183, Month 12, and Month 15 for incidence and severity of chronic GVHD. Extended evaluation continues at Months 18 and 24.
immuneMediatedToxicityMonitoring.notes: Any chronic GVHD reported as AESI within 24 hours

priorTherapyRequirements.name: Prior Kidney Transplant from Living Donor
priorTherapyRequirements.label: Living Donor Kidney Transplant
priorTherapyRequirements.description: Participants must have received a kidney transplant from a living donor 3 to 62 months prior to study enrollment. The same living kidney donor will undergo G-CSF mobilization and apheresis to generate the IF001 product for the study treatment.

priorTherapyRequirements.name: Limited Prior T Cell-Depleting Therapy
priorTherapyRequirements.label: No Extensive T Cell Depletion
priorTherapyRequirements.description: Participants enrolled in the RELIEF trial will be similar to those treated by DeZern et al. in that they will not have received extensive prior therapy with T cell-depleting agents or received multiple rounds of IS chemotherapies.
priorTherapyRequirements.prohibitedPriorEvents: Extensive prior therapy with T cell-depleting agents or multiple rounds of IS chemotherapies

stemCellCollectionRequirements.name: CD34+ Cell Dose Requirement
stemCellCollectionRequirements.label: Minimum CD34+ cells
stemCellCollectionRequirements.description: The cryopreserved IF001 product contains a minimum of 3 million CD34+ cells per kg of recipient ideal body weight (IBW) with no maximum limit. This minimum dose is set above the lowest dose given in the DeZern et al. (2023) trial, where all 20 patients conditioned with 400 cGy TBI achieved engraftment and stable long-term donor chimerism. Higher CD34+ cell doses are associated with faster neutrophil and platelet recovery and lower risk of graft failure.
stemCellCollectionRequirements.minimumYield: 3 million CD34+ cells per kg recipient IBW
stemCellCollectionRequirements.rationaleForMinimum: Set above the lowest dose in DeZern et al. (2023) trial where all patients achieved engraftment. Higher doses associated with faster recovery and lower graft failure risk.
stemCellCollectionRequirements.timing: Collection occurs after G-CSF mobilization of living kidney donor

stemCellCollectionRequirements.name: αβ TCR Cell Dose Requirement
stemCellCollectionRequirements.label: Target αβ TCR cells
stemCellCollectionRequirements.description: The IF001 product contains a target of 10 million αβ TCR cells per kg of recipient IBW (range 8-12 million per kg). This dose was chosen to minimize the incidence of severe acute or chronic GVHD while simultaneously reducing the incidence of graft failure and opportunistic infection. The dose balances risks of GVHD with high doses versus risks of non-engraftment and infection with low doses.
stemCellCollectionRequirements.minimumYield: 8 million αβ TCR cells per kg recipient IBW
stemCellCollectionRequirements.rationaleForMinimum: Chosen to minimize severe acute or chronic GVHD while reducing graft failure and opportunistic infection incidence.
stemCellCollectionRequirements.timing: Collection occurs after G-CSF mobilization of living kidney donor

siteManagement.name: RELIEF Study Site Management
siteManagement.label: Multicenter US Sites
siteManagement.siteType: Multiple centers in the United States
siteManagement.description: The study will be conducted at multiple centers in the United States. The Principal Investigator and at least 2 staff from each site will need to complete training requirements and obtain access to the Advantage eClinical electronic data capture system managed by Emmes. Site monitoring will be performed by Clinical Research Associates who will visit sites to check completeness of participant records, accuracy of CRF entries, adherence to protocol and Good Clinical Practice, progress of enrollment, and proper storage and administration of investigational product. Centers participating in this study must register pre- and post-HCT outcomes to the CIBMTR using procedures and forms of the Stem Cell Transplant Outcomes Database.

longTermFollowUp.name: Long-term Follow-up
longTermFollowUp.label: Long-term Follow-up
longTermFollowUp.description: Study participants who discontinue study treatment should not be considered withdrawn from the study and should return for follow-up assessments. Study completion is defined as the point at which all ongoing IF001 recipients have completed the Month 15 visit. The investigator must provide follow-up medical care for all participants who are prematurely withdrawn from the study or must refer them for appropriate ongoing care according to local practice. This includes reporting to the Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) and follow-up in appropriate national registries (eg, United Network for Organ Sharing, etc.). Centers participating in this study must register pre- and post-HCT outcomes to the CIBMTR using procedures and forms of the Stem Cell Transplant Outcomes Database. Federal legislation requires submission of these forms for all United States allotransplant recipients. The CIBMTR forms will be submitted directly to the CIBMTR through routine CIBMTR mechanisms.
longTermFollowUp.regulatoryBasis: Federal legislation requires submission of these forms for all United States allotransplant recipients
longTermFollowUp.infrastructure: Center for International Blood and Marrow Transplant Research (CIBMTR) and appropriate national registries (eg, United Network for Organ Sharing, etc.)
longTermFollowUp.notes: Site personnel will attempt to collect the vital status of the participant within legal and ethical boundaries for all participants enrolled, including those who did not receive IF001. Public sources may be searched for vital status information.
